claims.text: AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 forms a spinel-type oxide film under elevated-temperature tribological conditions.
The oxide film significantly improves degradation resistance relative to conventional alloys.
The AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 HEA is produced by inert-gas atomization followed by spark-plasma sintering.
The processed alloy has a multiphase microstructure containing two BCC phases and a minor sigma phase.
The intervention consists of elevated-temperature reciprocating wear testing.
The reciprocating wear tests are conducted in an oxidizing environment.
Testing spans approximately room temperature to 900 °C and uses an Al2O3 counterbody under cyclic reciprocating conditions.
High-temperature operation produces a dense and continuous surface oxide film.
Tribo-oxidation initiates in situ formation of the protective oxide layer.
The oxide layer shifts degradation from direct metal/solution attack to a diffusion-controlled process.
Formation of the oxide layer reduces wear depth.
Formation of the oxide layer reduces corrosion current density.
Wear depth decreases distinctly at 800 °C, and the highest wear resistance occurs at 900 °C.
At 800–900 °C, the alloy has lower wear depth than conventional alloys.
The coefficient of friction is reduced at high temperature relative to conventional alloys.
At 800–900 °C, the alloy has lower corrosion rates than conventional alloys.
At room temperature, a protective oxide film does not form to a significant extent.
Direct metal/solution contact causes higher room-temperature wear.
Excessive mechanical removal of the oxide film diminishes its protective effect.
Temperatures too low for oxide formation or substantial changes in the as-processed microstructure can diminish protection.

contradictions.description: The conditions and experiment specify an oxidizing atmosphere but no electrolyte or electrochemical cell, whereas the mechanism invokes metal/solution attack and the outcomes require corrosion-current-density measurements. The stated setup therefore does not operationalize the corrosion component of tribo-corrosion.
